transcript: We found two of the most theater adjacent things to do in London that aren't actually going to the theater. Morning of day four on my theatre trip to London, I headed over to Phantom Peak, which was an incredible open world game experience. It's like part immersive theatre, part escape room. You're solving mysteries and going on quests and playing games. It's sat in like an Old West style town and you can explore everything, you can talk to characters. I really went in knowing nothing about it and had the absolute best time because there's so much to do. It is extremely repeatable. We already want to go again. I have a full video debrief to come on this, but it was the best way to spend a Saturday afternoon. Afterwards we headed over to Borough Market to wander around, grab some food. Ended up at this insane pasta place that I highly, highly, highly recommend before we hopped on the train to head over to Stratford because we were seeing something that I have always wanted to do, ABBA Voyage. I love ABBA, and ABBA Voyage gives you a unique experience that literally no other band on the planet offers. Chance to see ABBA as they were in nineteen 79. They have created these incredible virtual avatars which looks so incredibly realistic that you forget they're not really there. Like you can see the pores in their skin and the sparkles on their costumes and there's a 10 piece live band. Just a remarkable concert experience all the way around. Everyone comes dressed up, it's an incredible late show and I got to sing along to all my favourite songs. And of course we ended the night back at my favourite place in London over churrs.
